---
title: "Database"
---

## Overview

The pipeline writes a SQLite database at `db_path` in `config/pipeline.yml` (default
`results/targets/stability.sqlite`). Bulky results -- loadings, scores, diagnostics, raw model
objects, projections -- are files under `stability_artifacts/<dataset_id>/` next to it, referenced
by paths relative to the DB's directory, so the two move together.

**It is a derived output.** Every row is rebuilt from the targets store; nothing is edited by
hand and there are no migrations.

- `db_<dataset>` (`write_dataset_db()`, `R/targets/db_write.R`) writes everything about one dataset
  in one transaction.
- `db_cross_dataset` (`write_cross_dataset_db()`) then writes the tables linking two datasets
  (projections, gene-space agreement) and deletes artifact files no row references.
- Other targets produce rows keyed by `fit_key` (dataset + method + parameters); the writers
  resolve keys to integer ids. Fits are upserted on `fit_key`, so a fit keeps its `fit_id` across
  rewrites.

**Schema versioning.** The schema is `R/db/schema.sql` and `R/db/views.sql`; `open_stability_db()`
(`R/db/connect.R`) creates them on a new file and stamps `PRAGMA user_version` with
`SCHEMA_VERSION`. It refuses a DB with a different version. After any schema change, bump
`SCHEMA_VERSION`, delete the DB and its `stability_artifacts/`, and run `tar_make()`; only the
ingestion and DB targets rerun.

**What it holds** for the 30 datasets (2026-10-05): 7,990 fits, 3.6 GB. The largest tables are
`match_scores` (8.9 M rows), `pattern_markers` (4.6 M), `gene_modules` (3.3 M), `factor_matches`
(3.0 M) and `enrichment_results` (2.1 M; their gene lists are about 1.1 GB of the file).

**Reading it.** Open read-only from R with
`DBI::dbConnect(RSQLite::SQLite(), path, flags = RSQLite::SQLITE_RO)`, or `sqlite3 -readonly`.
Whole-table scans of the 3.6 GB file over the cluster's network filesystem are slow from a login
node; copy it to a compute node's local disk for heavy queries.

### Design notes

- **Stability without every cell.** For each pair of fits of a method, factors are matched 1-to-1
  (Hungarian algorithm on loadings cosine; on |cosine| for methods whose factors can flip sign).
  Rather than store every factor × factor similarity (85% of which were never read), the DB keeps
  the matches plus context to judge them: each match's runner-up and margin, statistics of the
  unmatched similarities per fit pair, and pooled histograms.
- **WGCNA kME in context.** For each gene, its correlation with its own module's eigengene (kME),
  its best competing module, an analytic p-value, and an empirical p-value against a permutation
  null (each eigengene's samples shuffled 100 times), with member / non-member / permutation
  summaries and histograms per module. The full genes × modules kME matrix is an artifact.
- **Everything computed is kept,** including tables the app doesn't read yet (pattern drivers,
  markers, redundancy, ICASSO membership, the diagnostics).
- **Method-specific values in long tables** (`fit_params`, `fit_metrics`, `fit_artifacts`) rather
  than per-method columns.
- **Enrichment is stored separately from its jobs.** Each enrichment branch keeps its result
  trimmed to the significant terms; rows are built afterwards, so changing these tables never
  reruns fgsea.

## Conventions

- **Engine:** SQLite. Column types are SQLite storage classes: `INTEGER`, `REAL`, `TEXT`.
- **Booleans** are `INTEGER` with `CHECK (x IN (0,1))`.
- **Timestamps** are `TEXT` in ISO-8601 UTC (`utc_now()`, e.g. `2026-10-05T16:13:15Z`).
- **Creation:** the schema is defined in `R/db/schema.sql` (tables) and `R/db/views.sql`
  (views). `open_stability_db()` in `R/db/connect.R` creates them on a new DB and stamps
  `PRAGMA user_version`. An existing DB with a different version is refused; delete it and
  rebuild. There are no migrations.
- **Connection pragmas:** `foreign_keys = ON`, `journal_mode = WAL`, `synchronous = NORMAL`,
  `busy_timeout = 30000`.
- **Who writes:** the DB is written by two `deployment = "main"` targets only.
  - `db_<dataset>`, via `write_dataset_db()` in `R/targets/db_write.R`, writes every table
    scoped to one dataset in a single transaction.
  - `db_cross_dataset`, via `write_cross_dataset_db()` in `R/targets/db_write.R`, writes the
    tables that link two datasets (`projections`, `gene_space_agreement`).
  - Every other target computes in-memory rows keyed by `fit_key` (and `factor_index`). The
    writer resolves those keys to integer ids.
- **Update semantics:**
  - `datasets` and `fits` are upserted. `fits` is matched on `fit_key`, so a fit keeps its
    `fit_id` across rewrites.
  - All child rows of a dataset are deleted and re-inserted on each write.
  - Fits whose `fit_key` disappeared are deleted, and `ON DELETE CASCADE` removes their
    dependents.
- **Abbreviations below:** `PK` primary key, `FK → t.c` foreign key, `CASCADE` = `ON DELETE
  CASCADE`, `UQ` part of a UNIQUE constraint, `NN` NOT NULL, `IDX` indexed.

## Dataset-level tables

### `datasets`
One row per dataset (one input matrix and config, e.g. `EARLI`, `ANEMONES_DAY1`). It is the root
of every cascade. Its metadata columns record how to interpret the sample/feature metadata files,
which is what `dataset_metadata_sources` used to hold.

- **Rows from:** the `meta_<key>` (dataset config, via `read_dataset_metadata()` in
  `R/lib/metadata.R`) and `mat_<key>` (dimensions) targets.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()` (upsert).

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| dataset_id | TEXT | PK |
| description | TEXT | |
| n_samples | INTEGER | NN; columns of the analysed matrix |
| n_genes | INTEGER | NN; rows of the analysed matrix |
| sample_id_col | TEXT | |
| feature_id_col | TEXT | |
| ensembl_col | TEXT | |
| symbol_col | TEXT | |
| subject_id_col | TEXT | |
| sample_metadata_source | TEXT | original parquet path (provenance) |
| feature_metadata_source | TEXT | original parquet path (provenance) |
| written_at | TEXT | NN |

### `dataset_artifacts`
Paths, relative to the DB directory, of the files cached for a dataset: the analysed matrix and
the materialized sample/feature metadata.

- **Rows from:** the `matrix_file_<key>` and `metadata_files_<key>` file targets
  (`R/targets/projections.R::dataset_matrix_file()` and
  `R/targets/diagnostics.R::write_metadata_files()`). `kind` is the file name without `.rds`.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| dataset_id | TEXT | PK (with kind); FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE |
| kind | TEXT | PK (with dataset_id); CHECK IN ('matrix','sample_metadata','feature_metadata') |
| path | TEXT | NN |

### `matrix_diagnostics`
One row of sanity statistics per dataset for the analysed matrix: scale, skew/kurtosis,
conditioning and so on.

- **Rows from:** `matrix_diagnostics_<key>` (`R/targets/diagnostics.R::matrix_diagnostics_row()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| dataset_id | TEXT | PK; FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE |
| val_min | REAL | |
| val_max | REAL | |
| val_mean | REAL | |
| val_sd | REAL | |
| skew_p50 | REAL | median per-gene skewness |
| skew_p95 | REAL | 95th percentile per-gene skewness |
| kurtosis_p50 | REAL | median per-gene kurtosis |
| kurtosis_p95 | REAL | 95th percentile per-gene kurtosis |
| min_singular_value | REAL | |
| max_singular_value | REAL | |
| condition_number | REAL | |
| max_sample_cor | REAL | largest off-diagonal sample–sample correlation (duplicate check) |
| computed_at | TEXT | NN |

*(`n_genes` and `n_samples` moved to `datasets`.)*

## Method and fit tables

### `methods`
One row per method registry (`R/methods/<method>.R`). It holds the method properties that code
used to hardcode (`PARAM_GRID_METHODS`, `SIGN_AMBIGUOUS_METHODS`, method lists), so queries can
filter on them.

- **Rows from:** `METHOD_MANIFEST` (`R/lib/method_registry.R::discover_method_registries()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()` (upsert on `method`).

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| method | TEXT | PK |
| family | TEXT | NN; CHECK IN ('seed_sweep','param_grid') |
| sign_ambiguous | INTEGER | NN; boolean |
| has_loadings | INTEGER | NN; boolean (0 for WGCNA) |

### `fits`
One row per fitted model, i.e. one row of a method's parameter grid for one dataset. Failed fits
are recorded too, with `status = 'failed'` and the error message.

- `fit_key` is `<method>_<hash>`, the hash covering the dataset id, the method and the grid row's
  parameters, excluding `tar_group` and the method's `resource_params`
  (`R/targets/ingest.R::fit_key()`). It is the stable identity shared with the artifact file
  names, and it is unique across datasets.
- `fit_id` is the compact integer used in joins.
- **Rows from:** `ingest_<method>_<key>`
  (`R/targets/ingest.R::ingest_method_fits()`, which calls the method's
  `<method>_ingest$extract()` in `R/methods/<method>.R`). A fit that errored at fit time, or an
  sPCA fit stopped at its time limit (`error` = "killed_not_converged ..."), is a failed row. `representative` is set from `representatives_<method>_<key>`
  (`R/targets/ingest.R::representative_keys()`; sPCA from `selection_spca_<key>`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()` (upsert on `fit_key`).

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK |
| fit_key | TEXT | NN; UNIQUE |
| dataset_id | TEXT | NN; FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE; IDX (dataset_id, method, rank) |
| method | TEXT | NN; FK → methods.method |
| rank | INTEGER | number of factors requested (NULL for WGCNA) |
| seed | INTEGER | NULL for deterministic methods |
| bootstrap | INTEGER | NN; DEFAULT 0; boolean (ICA ICASSO resamples) |
| representative | INTEGER | NN; DEFAULT 0; boolean |
| mse | REAL | reconstruction MSE on the method's input matrix; NULL if not defined (sPCA) |
| n_factors | INTEGER | realized factors (WGCNA: non-zero modules) |
| status | TEXT | NN; CHECK IN ('ok','failed') |
| error | TEXT | error message when status = 'failed' (including "killed_not_converged" for sPCA fits stopped at `max_hours`) |
| written_at | TEXT | NN |

### `fit_params`
Every parameter of a fit's grid row as a long table, replacing the overloaded `alpha` column and
the parameters dropped by the current schema. Examples: sPCA `para`, `lambda`; WGCNA `power`,
`minModuleSize`, `networkType`; ICA `alpha`; CoGAPS `nIterations`. Resource settings
(`n.threads`, `nThreads`, `nSets`) are excluded.

- **Rows from:** `ingest_<method>_<key>` (`ingest_method_fits()`, from the registry `extract()`
  `params` field).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK (with name); FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| name | TEXT | PK (with fit_id); the tool's own argument name |
| num_value | REAL | set when the value is numeric |
| text_value | TEXT | set when the value is character/logical |

### `fit_metrics`
Method-specific scalar results for a fit:
- every method: `fit_seconds` (fit wall time).
- sPCA: `pev_sparse`, plus `pev_pca`, `prop_sparse`, `index_of_sparseness`, `is_selected` from
  the Index-of-Sparseness table.
- NMF: `n_iteration`, `target_loss`, `average_epochs`, `run_seconds`.
- CoGAPS: `mean_chisq`.
- ICA: `orthonormality_residual` (‖W Wᵀ − I‖), `prewhiten_var_retained`.
- WGCNA: `n_blocks` (1 when the network was built in one block), `n_unassigned`.

- **Rows from:** `ingest_<method>_<key>` (`<method>_ingest$extract()` `metrics`), plus
  `selection_spca_<key>` (`R/methods/spca.R::spca_select_fits()`) for the IS columns.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK (with name); FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| name | TEXT | PK (with fit_id) |
| value | REAL | |

### `fit_artifacts`
Paths, relative to the DB directory, of the per-fit files that hold the bulky results. Replaces
the nine `*_file` columns on `fits`.

| kind | Contents | Methods |
|---|---|---|
| loadings | genes × factors matrix | all except WGCNA |
| scores | samples × factors (WGCNA: eigengenes) | all |
| diag | method diagnostics list (PCA `sdev`/`center`/`mse_by_rank`; sPCA `pev`/`var_all`/`n_nonzero`/`center` + the rest of `spca()`'s output; ICA `W`/`K`/`A`/`S`/prewhitening rotation/`boot_idx`; CoGAPS SD matrices; NMF traces) | per method |
| raw | full native result object | CoGAPS (`CogapsResult`), WGCNA (`blockwiseModules()` output) |
| dendrogram | the gene tree the modules were cut from (`net$dendrograms[[1]]`; hclust pieces) | WGCNA (single block) |
| redundancy | K × K within-fit cosine matrix | nmf, cogaps, spca, ica (representatives) |
| kme | full genes × modules kME matrix | WGCNA |

- **Rows from:** `ingest_<method>_<key>` (loadings, scores, diag, raw, dendrogram),
  `redundancy_<method>_<key>` (redundancy), and `wgcna_fit_diag_<key>` (kme, via
  `R/targets/diagnostics.R::wgcna_fit_diagnostics()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK (with kind); FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| kind | TEXT | PK (with fit_id); CHECK IN ('loadings','scores','diag','raw','dendrogram','redundancy','kme') |
| path | TEXT | NN |

### `factors`
One row per latent factor of a fit: a component or pattern, or for WGCNA a non-zero module.

- Per-factor stability is the median matched |similarity| across same-rank fit pairs, per metric.
- ICA kurtosis lives here, replacing `ica_component_kurtosis`.
- **Rows from:** `ingest_<method>_<key>` (factor list and `factor_metrics`: kurtosis, n_genes),
  plus `pairs_<method>_<key>` (stability; `R/lib/ingest/pairs.R::factor_stability()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| factor_id | INTEGER | PK |
| fit_id | INTEGER | NN; FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE; UQ (fit_id, factor_index) |
| factor_index | INTEGER | NN; column position (WGCNA: module number) |
| label | TEXT | display label (e.g. `PC3`, `Pattern_2`, `ME5`) |
| n_genes | INTEGER | genes in the WGCNA module / sPCA non-zero loadings; NULL otherwise |
| stability_cosine | REAL | |
| stability_pearson | REAL | |
| stability_spearman | REAL | |
| kurtosis | REAL | ICA only |
| excess_kurtosis | REAL | ICA only |

## Pair-stability tables

Stability compares every pair of fits of one method within a dataset (all seeds, all ranks).

- Factor methods use Hungarian matching on loadings cosine (on |cosine| for sign-ambiguous
  methods). WGCNA matches modules by gene Jaccard.
- Instead of storing every factor × factor cell, the DB stores the matches plus enough
  unmatched-cell context (runner-up, null stats, histograms) to judge each match.
- Statistics over unmatched cells use |value|.
- **Rows from:** `pairs_<method>_<key>` (`R/targets/ingest.R::compute_method_pairs()`, which
  calls `R/lib/ingest/pairs.R::compute_factor_pairs()` or `compute_wgcna_pairs()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

### `fit_pairs`
One row per compared pair of fits of the same method and dataset, stored once with
`fit_a < fit_b`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_pair_id | INTEGER | PK |
| fit_a | INTEGER | NN; FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE; UQ (fit_a, fit_b) |
| fit_b | INTEGER | NN; FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE; IDX; CHECK (fit_a < fit_b) |
| same_rank | INTEGER | NN; boolean |
| n_factors_a | INTEGER | NN |
| n_factors_b | INTEGER | NN |
| ari | REAL | WGCNA only: adjusted Rand index of the module assignments |

### `factor_matches`
One row per Hungarian-matched factor pair within a fit pair: min(n_factors_a, n_factors_b) rows
per fit pair.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| match_id | INTEGER | PK |
| fit_pair_id | INTEGER | NN; FK → fit_pairs.fit_pair_id CASCADE; UQ (fit_pair_id, factor_a) |
| factor_a | INTEGER | NN; FK → factors.factor_id CASCADE; IDX |
| factor_b | INTEGER | NN; FK → factors.factor_id CASCADE; IDX |

### `match_scores`
The similarity of a matched pair under each metric, with its runner-up context.

- `runner_up` is the largest |value| among the unmatched cells in factor_a's row and factor_b's
  column.
- `margin` = |value| − runner_up. Positive means the match is clearly better than any
  alternative.
- Metrics: cosine, pearson and spearman for factor methods; jaccard for WGCNA.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| match_id | INTEGER | PK (with metric); FK → factor_matches.match_id CASCADE |
| metric | TEXT | PK (with match_id); CHECK IN ('cosine','pearson','spearman','jaccard') |
| value | REAL | NN; signed |
| runner_up | REAL | NULL when the fit pair has no unmatched cell in that row/column |
| margin | REAL | |

### `fit_pair_null`
Background ("null") distribution of the unmatched cells of one fit pair under one metric: the
similarity level a non-match reaches.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_pair_id | INTEGER | PK (with metric); FK → fit_pairs.fit_pair_id CASCADE |
| metric | TEXT | PK (with fit_pair_id); CHECK IN ('cosine','pearson','spearman','jaccard') |
| n | INTEGER | NN; number of unmatched cells |
| mean | REAL | |
| sd | REAL | |
| median | REAL | |
| p95 | REAL | |
| max | REAL | |

### `similarity_histograms`
Fixed-bin histograms (20 bins over |value| in [0, 1]) of matched and unmatched cells, pooled over
all fit pairs of a method at one pair of levels.

- `level` is `rank` for factor methods and `power` for WGCNA, with `level_a <= level_b`.
- These are the plotted distributions behind `fit_pair_null`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| dataset_id | TEXT | PK (all of: dataset_id, method, level_a, level_b, metric, bin); FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE |
| method | TEXT | PK; FK → methods.method |
| level_a | INTEGER | PK |
| level_b | INTEGER | PK |
| metric | TEXT | PK; CHECK IN ('cosine','pearson','spearman','jaccard') |
| bin | INTEGER | PK; 1–20 |
| bin_lo | REAL | NN |
| bin_hi | REAL | NN |
| n_matched | INTEGER | NN |
| n_unmatched | INTEGER | NN |

## WGCNA tables

### `gene_modules`
One row per gene per WGCNA fit: its module assignment (0 = unassigned) and its own-module kME,
with context.

- `next_module` / `kme_next` are the gene's best competing module.
- `p_analytic` is the Fisher-z p-value of `kme_own` with n = `datasets.n_samples`, as in
  `WGCNA::corPvalueStudent`.
- `p_perm` is the empirical p-value of `kme_own` against the module's permutation null (see
  `module_kme_summary`).
- The full genes × modules kME matrix is the fit's `kme` artifact.
- **Rows from:** `wgcna_fit_diag_<key>`, a dynamic branch per WGCNA fit
  (`R/targets/diagnostics.R::wgcna_fit_diagnostics()`). The module assignment comes from
  `ingest_wgcna_<key>`.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK (with gene); FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE; IDX (fit_id, module) |
| gene | TEXT | PK (with fit_id) |
| module | INTEGER | NN; 0 = unassigned |
| kme_own | REAL | NULL for module 0 |
| next_module | INTEGER | |
| kme_next | REAL | |
| margin | REAL | kme_own − kme_next |
| p_analytic | REAL | |
| p_perm | REAL | |

### `module_kme_summary`
Summary of kME against one module's eigengene, for three groups:
- `member`: genes in the module;
- `nonmember`: all other genes, the empirical background;
- `permutation`: all genes against `n_perm` sample-shuffled copies of the eigengene (the
  permutation null; default 100 permutations, seeded from `fit_key`).

- **Rows from:** `wgcna_fit_diag_<key>` (`wgcna_fit_diagnostics()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK (with module, grp); FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| module | INTEGER | PK |
| grp | TEXT | PK; CHECK IN ('member','nonmember','permutation') |
| n | INTEGER | NN |
| mean | REAL | |
| sd | REAL | |
| median | REAL | |
| p95 | REAL | |
| p99 | REAL | |

### `module_kme_histograms`
Fixed-bin kME histograms (40 bins on [−1, 1]) for the same three groups, used to plot a gene's
kME against its context.

- **Rows from:** `wgcna_fit_diag_<key>`.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK (with module, grp, bin); FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| module | INTEGER | PK |
| grp | TEXT | PK; CHECK IN ('member','nonmember','permutation') |
| bin | INTEGER | PK; 1–40 |
| bin_lo | REAL | NN |
| bin_hi | REAL | NN |
| count | INTEGER | NN |

### `wgcna_sft`
Dataset-level scale-free-topology fit (`WGCNA::pickSoftThreshold`) per candidate power, used to
choose the soft-thresholding power.

- **Rows from:** `wgcna_dataset_diag_<key>`
  (`R/targets/diagnostics.R::wgcna_dataset_diagnostics()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| dataset_id | TEXT | PK (with power); FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE |
| power | INTEGER | PK |
| sft_r_sq | REAL | |
| slope | REAL | |
| truncated_r_sq | REAL | |
| mean_k | REAL | |
| median_k | REAL | |
| max_k | REAL | |

### `gene_significance`
Per-gene association with each sample-metadata field: Spearman for numeric fields, Kruskal–Wallis
for categorical ones. Used for WGCNA gene-significance vs kME views.

- **Rows from:** `wgcna_dataset_diag_<key>` (`wgcna_dataset_diagnostics()`), using
  `sample_meta_<key>`.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| dataset_id | TEXT | PK (with field, gene); FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE |
| field | TEXT | PK; sample-metadata column |
| gene | TEXT | PK |
| test | TEXT | NN; CHECK IN ('spearman','kruskal') |
| statistic | REAL | |
| p_value | REAL | |

## ICA / ICASSO tables

ICASSO clusters the components of all ICA fits (seeds and bootstrap resamples) at one rank, to
assess which components recur.

- **Rows from:** `icasso_ica_<key>` (`R/targets/ingest.R::compute_method_icasso()`, which calls
  `R/lib/ingest/icasso.R`). That target also writes the dendrogram file with `fit_key` leaf
  labels.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

### `icasso_clusters`
One row per ICASSO cluster at a rank.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| dataset_id | TEXT | PK (with rank, cluster_id); FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE |
| rank | INTEGER | PK |
| cluster_id | INTEGER | PK |
| iq | REAL | cluster quality index (Iq) |
| n_members | INTEGER | NN |
| centrotype_factor_id | INTEGER | FK → factors.factor_id CASCADE |
| dendro_file | TEXT | relative path of the rank's dendrogram (same value on each row of a rank) |

### `icasso_membership`
Which ICASSO cluster each ICA component belongs to at its rank.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| factor_id | INTEGER | PK; FK → factors.factor_id CASCADE |
| dataset_id | TEXT | NN; FK (with rank, cluster_id) → icasso_clusters CASCADE |
| rank | INTEGER | NN |
| cluster_id | INTEGER | NN |
| intra_sim | REAL | the component's mean \|cosine\| to the other members of its cluster |

## Enrichment tables

### `enrichment_queries`
One row per enrichment query run for a factor: which test, and which gene direction.

- GSEA-type queries (`fgsea`, `gsea`) use `direction = 'both'`; a hit's sign comes from its NES.
- ORA-type queries are per direction.
- **Rows from:** `fgsea_<method>_<key>` (runs `R/ingest_jobs/fgsea_job.R`) and `wgcna_ora_<key>`
  (runs `R/ingest_jobs/wgcna_ora_job.R`), each branch storing its job's result trimmed to the
  significant terms (`R/targets/enrichment.R::trim_enrichment_result()`). `enrichment_<key>`
  (`enrichment_rows()`) turns them into rows, so a change to these tables never reruns the jobs.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| query_id | INTEGER | PK |
| factor_id | INTEGER | NN; FK → factors.factor_id CASCADE; UQ (factor_id, query_type, direction) |
| query_type | TEXT | NN; 'fgsea' (Hallmark GSEA), 'gsea' (GSEA against the other collections), 'cogaps_fora' (CoGAPS marker-gene ORA), 'ora' (top-100-gene ORA; WGCNA module ORA) |
| direction | TEXT | NN; CHECK IN ('pos','neg','both') |
| query_size | INTEGER | genes in the query set (ORA) / ranked list length (GSEA) |
| queried_at | TEXT | NN |

### `enrichment_results`
One row per enriched term for a query. ORA-only and GSEA-only columns are NULL for the other
type.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| query_id | INTEGER | PK (with term_id); FK → enrichment_queries.query_id CASCADE |
| term_id | TEXT | PK |
| source | TEXT | NN; MSigDB collection: 'HALLMARK', 'GO:BP', 'GO:MF', 'KEGG', 'REAC' or 'WP' |
| term_name | TEXT | |
| p_value | REAL | NN; fgsea's BH-adjusted p (`padj`); only terms with padj < 0.05 are stored; IDX (query_id, p_value) |
| intersection_size | INTEGER | |
| term_size | INTEGER | |
| nes | REAL | GSEA only |
| es | REAL | GSEA only |
| log2err | REAL | GSEA only |
| is_main_pathway | INTEGER | boolean; fgsea `collapsePathways` |
| genes | TEXT | JSON array (overlap / leading-edge genes) |

## Cross-dataset tables

Written by `db_cross_dataset` (`R/targets/db_write.R::write_cross_dataset_db()`). It runs after
every `db_<dataset>`, so fit ids on both sides are resolvable.

### `projections`
projectR projection of a source fit's loadings onto another dataset's matrix, either a related
timepoint (`within_dataset`) or another cohort (`cross_dataset`).

- The projected matrix is in the file at `path`.
- **Rows from:** `projectr_<key>`, one branch per (source dataset, target dataset)
  (`R/targets/projections.R::projection_rows()`, running `R/ingest_jobs/projectr_job.R`).

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| projection_id | INTEGER | PK |
| source_fit_id | INTEGER | NN; FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE; UQ (source_fit_id, target_dataset_id, include_intercept) |
| target_dataset_id | TEXT | NN; FK → datasets.dataset_id CASCADE; IDX |
| projection_type | TEXT | NN; CHECK IN ('within_dataset','cross_dataset') |
| include_intercept | INTEGER | NN; boolean |
| n_genes_matched | INTEGER | |
| n_samples | INTEGER | |
| mean_r_squared | REAL | |
| median_r_squared | REAL | |
| mean_pval | REAL | |
| median_pval | REAL | |
| mean_pvar | REAL | |
| median_pvar | REAL | |
| path | TEXT | NN; relative path of the projection result |

### `gene_space_agreement`
How similar two datasets' optimal fits of the same method are in gene space: the source fit's
loadings are projected onto the target fit's (projectR, shared Ensembl genes), and the mean
|matched projection| is reported. Computed in both directions for every pair of datasets in the
same family (`config/dataset_families.yml`).

- **Rows from:** `gene_space_<key>` (`R/targets/projections.R::gene_space_rows()`), with
  `<key>` as the source dataset.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| source_fit_id | INTEGER | PK (with target_fit_id); FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| target_fit_id | INTEGER | PK; FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| n_genes_matched | INTEGER | NN |
| mean_abs_diagonal | REAL | NN |

## Representative-fit analyses

These run on representative fits only (`fits.representative = 1`).

### `pattern_drivers`
projectionDriveR differential-gene results for one factor and one sample-metadata contrast. Full
results are in the file at `path`.

- **Rows from:** `drivers_<key>` (`R/lib/ingest/driver.R::pattern_driver_rows()`), using
  `sample_meta_<key>`.
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| driver_id | INTEGER | PK |
| factor_id | INTEGER | NN; FK → factors.factor_id CASCADE; UQ (factor_id, grouping_col, group1_level, group2_level, mode) |
| grouping_col | TEXT | NN |
| group1_level | TEXT | NN |
| group2_level | TEXT | NN |
| mode | TEXT | NN; CHECK IN ('CI','PV') |
| n_genes_considered | INTEGER | |
| n_significant_shared | INTEGER | |
| path | TEXT | NN |
| computed_at | TEXT | NN |

### `pattern_markers`
Marker genes per factor (patternMarkers-style scores), used to diagnose "too many patterns" (a
factor with no markers).

- **Rows from:** `redundancy_<method>_<key>` (`R/targets/ingest.R::compute_method_redundancy()`,
  which calls `R/lib/ingest/redundancy.R`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| factor_id | INTEGER | PK (with gene); FK → factors.factor_id CASCADE |
| gene | TEXT | PK |
| score | REAL | NN |

### `fit_redundancy`
Within-fit redundancy summary: off-diagonal cosine between a fit's own factors, and the number of
factors with no marker genes. The full K × K matrix is the fit's `redundancy` artifact.

- **Rows from:** `redundancy_<method>_<key>` (`compute_method_redundancy()`).
- **Written by:** `write_dataset_db()`.

| Column | Type | Attributes |
|---|---|---|
| fit_id | INTEGER | PK; FK → fits.fit_id CASCADE |
| max_offdiag_cosine | REAL | |
| median_offdiag_cosine | REAL | |
| n_factors_with_no_markers | INTEGER | |

## Views (`R/db/views.sql`)

| View | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `v_fits` | `fits` joined to `methods.family`, with the common `fit_params` (para, lambda, power, alpha) pivoted to columns |
| `v_factor_matches` | `factor_matches` + `match_scores` in both orientations (a→b and b→a), joined to fit and factor ids, rank, seed and dataset, so per-fit/per-factor stability queries need no direction UNION |
| `v_ingest_summary` | per (dataset, method): family, n_fits, n_ok, n_failed, last written_at; replaces the `ingests` table |
